summary: Anna Szabolcsi is a linguist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and earned her Ph.D. at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences. She served at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, as professor at UCLA (~1990–1998), and at New York University (~1999).
Anna Šebestová was an indologist and linguist who earned her Ph.D. at Charles University in 1919 under doctoral supervisor Josef Zubatý.

Anna-Pya Sjödin works in Indology and philosophy. She earned her PhD at Uppsala University in 2007, supervised by Gunilla Gren-Eklund, Eli Franco, Jonardon Ganeri, K. Venugopalan, and Toshihiro Wada, and also studied under Barbro Eriksson.
Annarao Kulkarni works in the fields of Indology and computational linguistics. He held posts at the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing and the Indian Heritage Language Computing Group.

Anncharlott Eschmann (1941–1977) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. She studied at Munich, Marburg, and Heidelberg University, earning her Ph.D. there in 1969 and serving as an assistant in 1975.
Anne Burchardi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Erik Haarh and held a post at the National Museum of Denmark.

Anne Carolyn Klein works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned degrees from Wisconsin-Madison (M.A.) and Virginia (Ph.D. under Jeffrey Hopkins), became Professor and Chair of Religious Studies at Rice University, and co-founded Dawn Mountain Center.

Anne E. Monius (1964–2019) was a religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned undergraduate and graduate degrees at Harvard. She taught at the University of Virginia (1997–2002) and became professor of South Asian Religions at Harvard in 2002.

Anne Feldhaus is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who earned her doctor's degree from the University of Pennsylvania. In 1981, she joined Arizona State University, becoming Distinguished Foundation Professor of Religious Studies and Emeritus Professor.
Anne Hardgrove is a historian and Indologist who studied at Carleton College and the University of Michigan. In 2000, she took up a post in history at the University of Texas at San Antonio.

Anne Hopkins Aitken (1911–1994) was a religious and Buddhist studies figure who studied at Scripps College, Northwestern, Stanford, and Oxford. She founded the Honolulu Diamond Sangha in 1959 and co-founded the Maui Zendo.

Anne M. Blackburn is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who attended the University of Chicago. She served as Assistant Professor of Religion at Cornell University (~2001–2021) before becoming a professor at Harvard University around 2021.

Anne MacDonald is an Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of British Columbia under Shotaro Iida. She held positions at the University of Vienna and became a professor at the Austrian Academy of Sciences in 2010.

Anne Nishimura Morse works in Japanology and history/archaeology, having studied under doctoral supervisor John M. Rosenfield. She held visiting scholar appointments at Smith College, Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties, Nara National Museum, and Kyoto National Museum.

Anne Ruth Hansen works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history. Having studied under Charles Hallisey, she held posts at the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where she became Professor of History.

Anne-Marie Blondeau is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar. She studied under Marcelle Lalou and Rolf Alfred Stein, among others, and held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 1982 and 2003).

Anne-Marie Esnoul (1908–1996) was an Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris and EPHE. She served at the Institut de Civilisation Indienne (1941–1966) and as directeur d’études at EPHE (1966–1977).

Anne-Marie Gaston (1941–2018) was a scholar in Indology, history and archaeology, and religious studies. She studied at the University of Oxford from approximately 1977 to 1982 under Alexis Sanderson and Richard Gombrich.
Annegret Bollée (1937–2021) was a linguist who pursued her studies at the University of Hamburg (~1957–1961), Aix-Marseille University (~1961–1962), and the University of Bonn (1969).

Annelies Kammenhuber (1922–1995) was a linguist and Indologist who completed her Ph.D. at Hamburg under Ferdinand Sommer. She was an assistant at Hamburg, an extraordinary professor at the Pontifical Biblical Institute, and an ordinary professor at Munich (1969–1987).
